memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium, a working hypothesis at Triaging. The case is parked on the return, not on the park rule: no D or F sits on management (C), business quality (C), predictability (the transmission, B) or trackability (the leading indicators, C). At 211.6 CHF (2026-09-21) the 'Modal return' on our path at a fair 21x 24-month-forward multiple is about minus 2.3 percent a year over eighteen months and about plus 2.9 percent a year over three years, about 7 percent a year even at today's 24.2x held, and the only combination that approaches the 20 percent bar (the consensus path with the multiple held, about 17.4 percent a year over eighteen months, a C) needs consensus right on both revenue and margin (possible, about 35 percent) and the multiple held given that (about 70 percent), about 25 percent together, unlikely. Two re-look triggers, either of which reopens the case: the price below about 155 CHF (the eighteen-month test) with the findings unchanged, about 135 CHF on the three-year test, about 150 CHF as the round level; or the cleared branch arriving (two consecutive quarters of mid-single-digit order growth in local currencies and FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 17.5 percent or more), at which point the fair anchor moves to 24x and the case clears the bar up to about 175 CHF on our path. The record's one-line bet: we are not betting at 211.6 CHF; if we were, we would be betting that a credible cost-out lands and the order book re-accelerates before a sector-driven multiple reverts, at odds of about one in four.
case: - The thesis in the record's words: Tecan is a self-help margin recovery under new hands, a 'Major Corporate Change' in a laboratory-automation business that lost a quarter of its revenue and 440 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin between 2022 and 2025. The change is real, funded and already producing savings. At 211.6 CHF the shares have paid for it in advance, and for a demand recovery the Q2 2026 order book did not show, so the 'Modal return' at a fair multiple is about minus 2 percent a year over eighteen months and about 3 percent a year over three years against a 20 percent bar.

- The change is internal and broad, and passes the framework's screen twice over (at least three strong forces, and chief-executive change plus a mid-term target set). Monica Manotas, 24 years at Thermo Fisher, became chief executive on 1 August 2025 after fifteen months on the board, replacing a six-and-a-half-year incumbent who presided over three guidance cuts in 2024, and acted within months: 'Rewired' launched March 2026 (four pillars; 2026 Reset, 2027 Recharge, 2028 Fully Rewired), the Boston design site closed April 2026, the California machining unit sold for USD 1 in March 2026 with a CHF 2.9m write-down, the Genomics activities exited, the NVIDIA collaboration signed March 2026, direct India set up in 2026. Camila Japur finance director from 1 June 2026; Matthias Gillner chairman from April 2026 with three new directors; the Partnering head seat interim under the chief executive from September 2025. The false-positive checks are clean: no caretaker chief executive, no 'PowerPoint transformation' (CHF 18.0m of savings booked in H1 2026, two sites exited, Penang cleared an FDA Class 3 inspection), no crown jewels sold, no dangerous leverage, a cash-funded buyback. Internal forces B: chief executive A, other leaders A, strategy B, standards B, perimeter B, shareholder returns B, guidance raised C (rebased, not raised), balance sheet C, geographies C, products C, price rises D, acquisitions D (Paramit impaired; acquisitions 72 percent of capital deployed 2019 to 2023; up to CHF 1.0bn of firepower unused), catch-all C (the ERP replacement, CHF 9.9m in H1 2026).

- The external forces net to neutral (C), so the case cannot lean on demand. Biopharma capital demand grew high-single-digit in local currencies in H1 2026 and China returned to mid-single-digit growth; academia and government fell double-digit on United States and European funding; the largest customer is guided slightly down for FY2026 with lower content per da Vinci 5 system; the franc costs about 60 basis points of margin a year at budget rates (120 basis points in H1 2026; each cent of USD/CHF is CHF 1.6m of operating margin); tariffs eased from about 100 basis points in 2025 to 40 for FY2026 under a 15 percent cap, with a CHF 6m IEEPA refund expected in H2 2026; competition is tightening (Hamilton described as having overtaken Tecan in high-end liquid handling on service; Chinese makers at about 25 percent of Tecan's price cited for 10 to 20 percent deal losses in Asia); material costs rose to CHF 191.8m in H1 2026 from CHF 184.1m on lower sales, at about 46 percent of sales. The company's own cycle has turned (B): sales fell 6.1, 13.0 and 5.5 percent in CHF in FY2023 to FY2025, then order entry grew 8.6 percent in H2 2025 and 6.7 percent in Q1 2026 before going flat in Q2 2026. Direction by force: demand mixed, competition a headwind, disruption two-sided, political and regulatory a small tailwind, supply side a headwind, the own cycle a tailwind, macro a headwind through the currency. The sector recovers faster than Tecan: Waters raised FY2026 organic growth guidance to 7 to 9 percent, Agilent grew 6.3 percent core, Sartorius 7.7 percent organic.
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, the bull case at its strongest: flat Q2 2026 orders were phasing (delayed Cavro shipments, biopharma budget timing, an easy Q1 comparison at the largest customer); H2 2026 and 2027 orders re-accelerate to mid single digits; 'Rewired' captures the full CHF 60m EBITDA gap to the 2028 target so that the margin reaches 20 percent on CHF 1bn of sales; the sell-side that sits at Hold with targets below the price is forced to upgrade twice; the multiple holds at the five-year median of 24x or re-rates toward the ten-year median of 26.4x as the life-science tools recovery broadens; and the shares deliver the 40 percent-plus return the bull case names. The evidence for it: order entry positive in local currencies for three consecutive periods with a book-to-bill above one; an 80 basis point H1 2026 margin beat on savings that are itemised and structural; management guiding to the upper end and Penang FDA-cleared with the footprint moves on schedule; Asia-Pacific up 34.2 percent in local currencies; consumables at 64.4 percent of Life Sciences sales; net cash and a buyback; UBS at CHF 11.11 of FY2028 EPS and a 222 CHF target; the tariff drag halved and a CHF 6m refund coming; Waters, Agilent and Sartorius all beating and raising. The record concedes: the cost-out is credible and half of the FY2026 bridge is banked; the balance sheet, the operator and the recurring base are real; on the consensus path with the multiple held the eighteen-month return is about 17 percent a year, a C and within reach of the bar; and if the cleared branch arrives, 24x is the fair anchor and the price at which the case clears the bar rises to about 175 CHF on our path and about 200 CHF on consensus. The record holds because the outcome that clears the bar today needs consensus right on both revenue and margin (possible, about 35 percent) and the multiple held given that (about 70 percent), about 25 percent together; because the last print points the other way on the demand leg (Q2 orders flat, the largest customer guided down, academia falling double-digit, United States organic growth about 1 percent); because the shares stand above four of five brokers' targets, so the upgrades the bull needs must come from a sell-side that sees 10 to 20 percent downside; and because the framework's answer to a case that is compelling only once the event has happened is to wait for the price, not the event. Where the case against would win: a Q3 2026 trading update with order growth of 5 percent or more in local currencies, followed by FY2027 margin guidance of 17.5 percent or more.

- At Building Block 2, the Risks research's "false friend", the only hypothesis in its matrix with no hard inconsistency: the order recoveries of H2 2025 and Q1 2026 are safety-stock and re-ordering spikes that mask structural share loss in direct Life Sciences and a mix shift toward low-margin contract manufacturing, so the gross margin stays pinned at 35 percent or below, the 2028 margin target is missed by 200 to 400 basis points, and the largest customer's transition to lower-content systems or in-sourcing removes up to a fifth of group revenue with little warning. The evidence for it since the report: the H1 2026 gross margin fell to 33.9 percent, Q2 orders were flat, the largest customer's FY2026 sales are guided slightly below FY2025, and United States Life Sciences organic growth was about 1 percent. The record concedes the mix and margin points in full and the customer-concentration point as a fragility, which is why business quality is a C and not a B. It holds a C rather than a D because the H1 2026 print does not show structural share loss: direct Life Sciences grew 4.6 percent in local currencies in Q2 with consumables rising to 64.4 percent of segment sales, Asia-Pacific grew 34.2 percent on share gains in China, Abbott Molecular brought manufacturing back, and the margin rose 180 basis points underlying on itemised savings. The foundations are fragile where the report says; they are not failing.
triggers: - Order intake ('Case/SP Key Driver'): confirm at mid-single-digit group order growth in local currencies for two consecutive quarters (H2 2026 and Q1 2027); a Q3 2026 trading update with order growth of 5 percent or more moves the demand leg to probable; alarm at a second consecutive quarter at or below 0 percent; invalidate at two consecutive quarters negative or a book-to-bill below 0.95x; a second flat quarter puts the FY2027 revenue consensus of plus 5.0 percent in doubt. Our modal H2 2026: plus 3 to 5 percent.

- The 'Rewired' cost bridge ('Case/SP Key Driver'): FY2026 delivered at 16.5 percent or above with FY2027 guidance of 17.5 percent or more moves the margin leg to probable; alarm at FY2026 below 16.0 percent or FY2027 guidance below 17.0 percent; invalidate at a FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin below 16.5 percent; savings tracked against CHF 25m to 35m, CHF 18.0m booked.

- The multiple ('Case/SP Key Risk'): the 24-month-forward P/E against the 21x anchor, the 19x two-year median and the 17.55x five-year 10th percentile; the price against about 155 CHF; reversion toward 21x probable (about 60 percent) within eighteen months.

- The largest customer ('Case/SP Key Risk'): alarm at a fall of more than 10 percent in FY2026 sales to the customer (the Risks research's alarm below CHF 164m a year); invalidate at an announced in-sourcing or design-out of Tecan content; probable (about 65 percent) that volumes are stable to slightly down through FY2027.

- The Swiss franc ('Case/SP Key Risk'): USD/CHF and EUR/CHF against the 0.80 and 0.92 budget rates; alarm below 0.75 or 0.88; invalidate at USD/CHF below 0.70 sustained for a half; USD/CHF back above 0.82 for a half would change our mind the other way.
- Gross margin recovery: alarm below 34 percent in H2 2026; invalidate below 33 percent for a full year; refute the case at a gross margin below 34 percent for a further half.
